text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- PITTA WINS EASILY; SOCIAL DEMOCRATS HAVE WEAK SHOWING

Celso Pitta, the candidate of Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf, was close to the magic number that would give him a first-round win in mayoral elections but the suspense continued until this newspaper went to bed early this morning.
-- REAL CURRENCY HAS LARGEST EXPANSION SINCE CHRISTMAS 1995

Brazil's monetary base posted in September its greatest expansion in 10 months as banks made a last-minute run on the rediscount rate and injections of resources prompted by the Central Bank, offsetting a net outflow of close to $1.0 billion.
-- VALE WILL BE CONTROLLED BY A HOLDING COMPANY

The government will reveal Monday, when it releases the sale terms for Vale do Rio Doce, the creation of a Special Purpose Company to administer the state mining giant for five years after its privatization.
O GLOBO
-- IN RIO MAYOR'S RACE, CONDE AND CABRAL FACE RUNOFF ROUND

Rio de Janeiro mayoral candidates Luiz Conde of the Liberal Front Party and Sergio Cabral of the Social Democratic Party will go to a second, runoff round in mid-November, according to elections officials.
-- THE BATTLE IN SAO PAULO IS BETWEEN PITTA AND ERUNDINA
Celso Pitta of the Progressive Party and Luisa Erundina of the Worker's Party will face a runoff in November in the race for Sao Paulo mayor.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- PARCIAL VOTE COUNT SHOWS PITTA, ERUNDINA IN RUNOFF
Celso Pitta and Luiza Erundina should square off in a second runoff round of voting for mayor of Sao Paulo on Nov. 15, according to results released by the Regional Elections Tribunal.
-- SAO PAULO MAYOR MALUF TO OPPOSE PRESIDENT'S RE-ELECTION

Emboldened by the strong showing for his mayoral candidate Celso Pitta, Sao Paulo Mayor Paulo Maluf vowed he would oppose a proposed constitutional amendment thaqt would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election in 1998.
-- RESULTS DEEPEN RIFT BETWEEN CARDOSO'S PARTY AND RIGHTISTS
The results of Thursday's municipal elections deepens the rift between President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's Social Democratic Party and the rightist Liberal Front Party.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
